criteria.verified: Committed under plugin/skills/faffter-dark-spec-review/eval/in-spec-ratification/: three decision variants, the implementation-level fixture, the scope-test objection set, the register fixture, a README and run-log.

criteria.ac: **Pin every run variable except the tag, and record the pin.** Items 1-3 below compare outcomes across fixture variants that must differ in exactly the tag — so every run pins the same backend/model identity, the same `--context` file set, and the same `## Ratified scope` presence-or-absence. Record the pinned values in a `run-log.md` (or equivalent) committed alongside the fixture trio itself — one file per fixture-directory, not a separate untracked note — so a later re-run of the fixture has the exact prior pin to reproduce, and a PR reviewer can check the pin without re-deriving it. A pass whose runs used different backends or context, or whose pin was never recorded, is not evidence the tag caused the difference.
criteria.verified: run-log.md records the single-element pinned chain, timeout, max-tokens, deadline, empty context set, absent Ratified-scope block, lens and system-dir, committed beside the fixtures.

criteria.ac: **Test coverage item 1 (no regression):** run the design lens(es) against the **untagged** decision-level fixture, pinned per the rule above; the same `major` (or higher) objection appears. This is the fixture's pinned baseline, not a fresh eyeball check.
criteria.verified: Item 1 ran and the major objection appeared; recorded in run-log.md.

criteria.ac: **Test coverage item 2 (defers to observation):** run the same lens(es), same pinned run variables, against the **tagged** decision-level fixture with no `## Ratified scope` file present; the previously-gating objection now appears only as an `observation` citing the tagged line. Because both variants differ in exactly one suffix under otherwise-pinned conditions, a pass here is direct evidence the tag — not lens variance — caused the downgrade.
criteria.verified: Item 2 ran and the objection appeared only as an observation citing the tagged line; the implementation-level objection stayed major, so the downgrade was scoped.

criteria.ac: **Test coverage item 3 (critical never deferred):** the **critical**-severity fixture variant, tag present, same pinned run variables; confirm it still gates.
criteria.verified: Item 3 ran and the critical still gated with the tag present.

criteria.ac: **Test coverage item 4 (scope test correctly declines an implementation objection — the false-negative direction):** run the ratify-offer scope test (Decision 2) against the separate implementation-level fixture's objection; confirm it is classified as implementation-level and the ratify choice is **not** offered. This closes the false-negative gap a decision-only fixture pair cannot exercise: a scope test that always classifies "decision-level" would pass items 1-3 while still wrongly ratifying every implementation objection.
criteria.verified: Item 4 ran: the implementation-level claim classified `implementation-level`, `ratify_offered=no`.

criteria.ac: **Test coverage item 5 (the fail-safe middle is tested, not merely named):** run the same scope test against the *ambiguous* worked example itself ("Postgres is fine, but this schema will lock the table under load" — Decision 2's third worked example, not the clean implementation case item 4 uses) and confirm it too is **not** offered ratify. Item 4 alone tests only the unambiguous implementation case; the "ambiguous → no ratify, never the reverse" safety claim is specifically about the boundary case, so the boundary case is what must be exercised — a scope test that classifies unambiguous cases correctly but defaults an ambiguous one to "decision-level" would pass item 4 while failing the exact case the asymmetry exists to protect.
criteria.verified: Item 5 ran: the ambiguous worked example classified `ambiguous`, `ratify_offered=no`. A decision-level positive control returned yes, so the test is not a constant no.
